definition: The practice of taking a model trained on one task or dataset and adapting it to a different but related task, leveraging previously learned representations.
details: Transfer learning underlies the modern pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm, allowing models to reuse general knowledge learned from large datasets rather than learning every task from scratch.

explainer.lead: Transfer learning takes a model trained on one task or dataset and adapts it to a different but related task, reusing learned representations. It underpins the modern pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm, so models need not learn every task from scratch.

tiers.eli5: You learn to ride a bike, then pick up a scooter quickly because much of the balance skill carries over.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pretrain on large data, then fine-tune on the target task. The pitfall is that a source task too unrelated to the target can yield little useful reuse.
tiers.paperLevel: Taking a model trained on one task or dataset and adapting it to a different but related task, leveraging previously learned representations. It allows reuse of general knowledge from large datasets instead of learning each task from scratch.

explainer.example: A model pretrained on large text is fine-tuned on a smaller task-specific dataset instead of being trained from scratch.
